Source: On physical exam, he is found to have a 3 cm full-thickness defect in the abdominal wall to the right of the umbilicus with evisceration of a loop of the bowel.
His weight is 3.0 kg (6.6 lb), and his height and his head circumference are in the 30th and 40th percentiles, respectively.
The mother declined all prenatal screening tests during this pregnancy.
His temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 63/41 mmHg, pulse is 133/min, and respirations are 39/min.
The mother initially labored at home with a midwife but was transferred to the hospital for failure to progress.
A 1-hour-old newborn boy is evaluated in the delivery room.
The abdominal defect is immediately covered in sterile saline dressings and an orogastric tube and 2 peripheral intravenous lines are placed.
His Apgar scores were 7 and 8 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively.
The infant was eventually delivered via Caesarean section.
He was born at 37 weeks gestation to a 39-year-old G3P3 mother.
